children: Shares of social network operator Meta Platforms

jumped 4.8% in the morning session after JPMorgan added the company to its Analyst Focus List, designating it a preferred internet pick alongside Amazon on strengthening artificial intelligence-driven advertising momentum.

JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth removed Alphabet from the focus list in favor of Meta, writing in a note to clients cited by CNBC that recent results highlighted widening operational outperformance in digital ads.The advance was also supported by a broader relief rally.

The major indices rebounded with the tech heavy Nasdaq index up more than 2% in the morning session as dip buyers stepped in following a severe rout driven by artificial intelligence names in the previous week.
The shares were trading at $640.04, up 4.9% from the previous close.
What is the market telling us

Meta’s shares are quite volatile and have had 16 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 18 days ago when the stock dropped 5.7% on the news that pre-market gains were erased, as surging artificial intelligence capital expenditures overshadowed better-than-expected third-quarter revenue and fourth-quarter guidance.

Meta is down 1.6% since the beginning of the year, and at $640.04 per share, it is trading 17.7% below its 52-week high of $777.59 from September 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Meta’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,908.
